name: Summit Block Scramble (from Stehekin)
approach: McGregor Mountain is only reachable via Stehekin, at the head of Lake Chelan, which has no outside road access — get there by the Lady of the Lake ferry, floatplane, or the long trail from Cascade Pass/Bridge Creek. From Stehekin Landing, take the NPS shuttle bus (or walk/bike) 11 miles up the Stehekin Valley Road to its end at High Bridge (a hiking permit is required for the overnight version of this trip). From High Bridge, follow the Old Wagon Road/PCT north to Howard Lake at about 1.3 miles; the signed junction where the McGregor Mountain Trail forks right is just beyond the lake — Howard Lake is a reliable water source and a good gut-check that you're on route. Beyond the lake the trail switchbacks relentlessly (climbers report close to 100 switchbacks) up through forest and rocky slopes that get hot and dry with little shade or water, gaining well over 5,000 ft over the next 5.5-6 miles to Heaton Camp at about 6,700 ft (mile 6.8 of 7.7), a small single-party designated site where a seasonal-snowmelt stream just below camp is the last dependable water before the summit push. From Heaton Camp the maintained trail continues another quarter- to half-mile to where it ends at the base of a talus field; total stats to the true summit are 7.7 miles and 6,600 ft one-way. The final roughly 1,000-1,100 vertical feet is an exposed Class 2-3 scramble, not a trail: intermittent (and often faded) red arrows painted on the rock mark the line, which loops right then left behind a lower sub-summit, crosses a snowfield/talus shelf above the Sandalee Glacier, then follows a fairly level shoulder past an old radio installation to the true summit and former fire-lookout site. Carry an ice axe if snow still covers the talus or the shelf above the glacier (common into midsummer), and expect loose rock ('kitty litter' on slabs) and real exposure on the ledges near the top — staying precisely on the arrow-marked line matters, as it gets noticeably dicier off-route.
